issues.title: Compact sparse filtered scan output into fuller chunks within a morsel
issues.hypothesis: In q02 the partsupp scan with the pushed bloom filter emits 73,008 rows out of 8M, which is about 18 rows per 2048-row vector. TableScanFunc (table_scan.cpp:316) returns every non-empty vector as its own DataChunk, so about 3,900 tiny chunks go through the pipeline. The first hash-join probe (p_partkey) shows 0.02-0.03s cumulative for only 73k probe rows. That is per-chunk overhead (hashing setup, ScanStructure init, operator dispatch), not per-row work. Measured with threads=8 hot: the 1-column BF scan is 0.06s and the HJ probe 0.01-0.02s, while a full unfiltered 3-column scan of partsupp takes only 1.6ms wall. Downstream joins are CachingPhysicalOperators and already coalesce their outputs, so the first operator after a selective scan is the one that pays. E0002 (a faster BitPacking select) showed no official gain, which suggests decode is not the bottleneck. Per-chunk overhead is the next suspect.
issues.plan: In the parallel DuckTableScanState::TableScanFunc (src/function/table/table_scan.cpp, around line 316), when the scan has table filters and storage.Scan returns a chunk with 0 < size < STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE/8, do not return it straight away. Copy it into a per-local-state buffer DataChunk of the output types (add a `DataChunk compact_buffer` to TableScanLocalState, initialised lazily with output.GetTypes()). Keep calling storage.Scan for the same morsel only (do NOT call NextParallelScan while the buffer is non-empty, so batch-index and insertion-order semantics are kept). Append each result with DataChunk::Append. Stop when the buffer holds >= STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE/2 rows, when the next chunk would overflow STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE (in that case emit the buffer and keep the pending chunk for the next call, or simply stop before appending a chunk that does not fit), or when the morsel is exhausted (Scan returns 0). Then output.Move/Reference the buffer. If a chunk of size >= STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE/8 arrives while the buffer is empty, return it unchanged (fast path, no copy). Handle the CanRemoveFilterColumns path by compacting after ReferenceColumns, and skip compaction for is_create_index. Keep the TASK_EXECUTOR async return logic unchanged: only return HAVE_MORE_OUTPUT/FINISHED after the buffer has been flushed. Verify that row-id/virtual columns come through Append correctly, and that the DataTable scan state lifetimes stay valid: strings are deep-copied by Append into the buffer's own heap.
issues.expected_gain: q02: about 0.02-0.03s cumulative CPU on the first probe after the partsupp scan, plus less pipeline dispatch overhead. Estimated 4-8% wall. Also helps the supplier and part scans when they are selective (part: 8,061 of 2M rows).
issues.generality: Any query whose table scan has a selective pushed filter (static predicates, bloom/IN join filters, LIKE) feeding joins, aggregates or projections. That is common in star-schema and TPC-H/DS style workloads. Queries could get slower when filters keep roughly 5-12% of rows (the copy cost of Append, including string deep-copies, without much overhead saved). The 1/8-vector trigger limits this. Scans without filters are unaffected.
issues.risk: Medium-low. Correctness depends on not crossing morsel boundaries (batch index/order preservation) and on properly flushing the buffer at the end of the morsel and the scan. Wrong async-mode handling could drop or duplicate rows. The copy of string columns adds some cost.
